# T008 — Backend HTTP dependency remediation

## Summary

On 2026-10-21, updated the backend to Express **4.22.3** (not Express 5) and direct body-parser **1.20.8**. npm regenerated both the root workspace and independent backend locks. Both now resolve proxy-addr **2.0.8**, path-to-regexp **0.1.13**, and qs **6.16.1**. The Express-related findings, including the critical proxy-addr finding, are absent from both final audits. The scanner still reports other, open findings.

## Changes

- `backend/package.json`: pin the patched Express 4 parent and directly used body-parser 1.x; no route, proxy setting, or production code change.
- `package-lock.json`, `backend/package-lock.json`: regenerate with npm, then explicitly refresh the independent lock's in-range proxy-addr with `npm update proxy-addr --prefix backend --workspaces=false --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`. Root npm re-hoisted the HTTP package subtree; the backend lock retains its separate installation graph. No lockfile was hand-edited.
- `test/backend-characterization.test.mjs`: resolve Express relative to the backend package, rather than assuming `backend/node_modules/express` exists. The production server and test now reference the same instance regardless of npm hoisting; all existing route assertions remain unchanged.

## Decisions

Native npm audit JSON and the [GitHub proxy-addr advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h) identify 2.0.8 as patched. npm registry `npm view express@4.22.3 dependencies --json` confirms Express 4.22.3 permits patched proxy-addr 2.0.8, requires path-to-regexp `~0.1.13`, and admits qs 6.16.x and body-parser 1.20.8. Express 4.22.2 still specified path-to-regexp `~0.1.12` and qs `~6.15.1`; 4.22.3 is the smallest suitable Express 4 parent according to the current audit (`express` affected through 4.22.2). No forced audit fix, overrides, major upgrades, suppression, or change to Express `trust proxy` was used. `backend/server.js` has no explicit `trust proxy` setting; the proxy-addr advisory's mapped-IPv6 trust-subnet misconfiguration is not established here, but removing vulnerable code is appropriate. Routing regexes and query/body parsing remain reachable via the backend HTTP routes. Other remaining findings are not accepted or waived by this task.

## Follow-ups and risks

Both scans still show critical `fast-xml-parser` and other Azure SDK, tooling, frontend, and backend findings assigned to subsequent approved tasks. Offline characterization confirms HTTP routes, but not deployment-specific proxy configurations or a live Azure service. An intermediate test run after standalone backend installation encountered npm hoisting assumptions in the test fixture; the fixture was repaired and the final post-edit root suite passed in full. Existing build/lint warnings were not suppressed.
